hook: A town pool could stay open every evening of the week. Each extra hour gives swimmers some benefit and costs the town a lifeguard, heat and light. Open too few hours and good evenings go to waste; open too many and the town pays for empty lanes. There is one best number of hours, and it is found at the margin.

chain.cause: A unit's MSB is greater than its MSC
chain.effect: making it adds to total surplus

chain.cause: Units are added until MSB = MSC
chain.effect: total surplus is as large as it can be: the efficient quantity

chain.cause: A policy or market power moves quantity away from that point
chain.effect: units are lost (or wasted) whose benefit and cost do not match

chain.cause: Those units' net benefit is lost
chain.effect: deadweight loss appears: a market failure if the market itself causes it

ideas: Marginal social benefit (MSB) is the benefit of one more unit to everyone; marginal social cost (MSC) is its cost to everyone.
The socially efficient quantity is where MSB = MSC. There total surplus is largest.
A competitive market whose demand and supply capture every benefit and cost has D = MSB and S = MSC, so its equilibrium is efficient.
Any other quantity leaves deadweight loss, a triangle between MSB and MSC pointing toward the efficient quantity. A market failure is a market outcome that is not efficient.

misconception.wrong: A market equilibrium is always the socially efficient outcome.
misconception.right: It is efficient only when demand captures every benefit and supply every cost, and buyers and sellers are price takers. Market power, and benefits or costs that fall on others, make the market quantity differ from MSB = MSC.

summary: A quantity is socially efficient where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost: every unit worth more than it costs is made, and no other. Total surplus is largest there. A competitive market in which demand and supply reflect all benefits and costs reaches that point on its own. Taxes, subsidies, price controls and monopoly move the quantity away from it, and the lost net benefit is deadweight loss, a triangle between MSB and MSC that points toward the efficient quantity. A market outcome that is not efficient is a market failure.
